label: <DEL> step when the first two original tokens are from {w,n,e,r,z,l,x,k,g,y,s,t}
explanation: Almost exclusively a delimiter-step unit: 98.8% of activation mass is at the <DEL> step (t = L), where the model starts outputting original token 0. It never fires in the copy phase; the small remainder is in the late original phase, mostly on input j. At <DEL>, how often it fires and how strongly is graded by the identity of the first original token (out_tok = orig(0)): w is strongest (about half of w-initial sequences fire, and w heads the top examples), followed by n, e, r, z, l, x, k, then g, y, s, t. The second original token (next_out) also matters, with roughly the same preference order (w, r, k, n, e, l, x, g). Activation is higher when L is larger (rate goes from 0.8% at to_go=3 to 9.5% at to_go=8) and somewhat lower when there are more digits in the sequence. Requiring both of the first two tokens to be in the preferred set gives dev F1 0.67 and mass recall 0.84. It looks like a graded, roughly additive readout of orig(0) and orig(1) with an L-dependent bias, so no single crisp boolean captures it. It does not fire at <DEL> for sequences that start with other letters (a, b, c, d, ...) or with digits, unless the activation is weak.
